apply: git apply --check <patch>, then git apply <patch>, at the consumer repository root (git-style a/ b/ repository-relative paths). The text before the first 'diff --git' line is a description that git apply ignores.
scope_rule: Each patch changes only (a) the affected source line and its explanatory comment and (b) the consumer's own bundled test fixture data, replaced by the proposed variant byte for byte, because a migration pinned to the proposed contract must be tested against proposed responses. Test assertions and business expectations are never changed, and unrelated conversions and negative controls stay untouched.
deployment_caveat: The patch is pinned to the proposed contract: it is not backward compatible with current-contract responses unless made version-aware, so its deployment must be coordinated with the provider's cutover.
deployment_assumption: A migration validated against proposed responses is not automatically safe to deploy before the provider change: against baseline (current-contract) responses the migrated code fails the same unchanged business assertion. That run is recorded as deployment-assumption evidence, never as a regression.
validation_runner: Local test runs in tests/demo/test_migrations.py with the LOCAL RUNNER DOUBLE's standing: trusted local fixtures; plain subprocess; not a sandbox; not Sai's runner. Each run uses a temporary git-initialized copy of the template and the consumer's own test command.
validation_scope: Validated within the tested scope only: the consumer's own suite with its bundled USD whole-dollar fixtures (baseline and proposed variants). This does not establish correctness for other amounts, currencies or code paths.
